questions.question: Which two signs can be interchanged so as to balance the given equation? 72 ÷ 36 + 12 × 13 - 48 = 63
questions.questionHtml:
Which two signs can be interchanged so as to balance the given equation?

72 ÷ 36 + 12 × 13 - 48 = 63
questions.solution:
BODMAS RULE:

Option (1): × and ÷

Given equation: 72 ÷ 36 + 12 × 13 - 48 = 63

Interchanged equation is : 72 × 36 + 12 ÷ 13 - 48 = 63

⇒  72  × 36+ 0.92 - 48 = 63

⇒ 2592 + 0.92 - 48 = 63

⇒ 2592.92 - 48  = 63

⇒ 2544.92 ≠ 63

⇒ LHS ≠ RHS

Option (2): + and -

Given equation: 72 ÷ 36 + 12 × 13 - 48 = 63

Interchanged equation is: 72 ÷ 36 - 12 × 13 + 48 = 63

⇒ 2 - 12 × 13 + 48 = 63 

⇒ 2 - 156 + 48 = 63

⇒ 2 + 48 - 156 = 63 

⇒ 50 - 156 = 63

⇒ -106 ≠ 63

⇒ LHS ≠ RHS

Option (3): + and ÷

Given equation: 72 ÷ 36 + 12 × 13 - 48 = 63

Interchanged equation is: 72 + 36 ÷ 12 × 13 - 48 = 63

⇒ 72 + 3 × 13 - 48 = 63

⇒ 72 + 39 - 48 = 63

⇒ 111 - 48 = 63

⇒ 63 = 63

⇒ LHS = RHS

Option (4): × and -

Given equation: 72 ÷ 36 + 12 × 13 - 48 = 63

Interchanged equation is: 72 ÷ 36 + 12 - 13 × 48 = 63

⇒ 2 + 12 - 13 × 48 = 63

⇒ 2 + 12 - 624 = 63

⇒ 14 - 624 = 63

⇒ - 610 ≠ 63

⇒ LHS ≠ RHS

Hence, the correct answer is "+ and ÷".

questions.question: What will be the net discount percentage of three successive discounts of 30%, 20%, and 10% on a product?
questions.questionHtml: What will be the net discount percentage of three successive discounts of 30%, 20%, and 10% on a product?
questions.solution:
Given:

Successive discounts of 30%, 20%, and 10% on a product.

SP = (1 – d1/100) x (1 – d2/100) x (1 – d3/100) 

Let initial price be Rs. 100

From the problem statement, price after 3 successive discounts can be written as

 final price = 100 × (1 – 20/100) × (1 – 10/100) × (1 – 30/100)

final price = 100 × (0.8) × (0.9) × (0.7)

final price = Rs. 50.4

 Discount is 100 – 50.4 = Rs. 49.6

∴ the net discount is 49.6%

Hence, the correct answer is "49.6%".

Alternate MethodThree successive discounts of 30%, 20%, and 10% on a product

⇒ 30 + 20 - 30 × 20/100

⇒ 44%

Successive discount on 44% and 10%

⇒ 44 + 10 - 44 × 10/100

⇒ 49.6%

Hence, the correct answer is "49.6%".

questions.question: In the following question, select the odd word pair from the given alternatives.
questions.questionHtml: In the following question, select the odd word pair from the given alternatives.
questions.solution:
In the pairs "Question - Answer", "Cup - Saucer", and "Chair - Table", the two words are directly related and often used together in a complementary way.

A question is often followed by an answer.

  • A cup is often placed on a saucer.
  • A chair is often paired with a table.

However, the pair "Pencil - Rub" doesn't follow the same pattern of complementary use. While you might use an eraser (not 'rub') to remove pencil markings, the word 'rub' itself doesn't have a direct, complementary relationship to 'pencil'. Therefore, "Pencil - Rub" is the odd one out.

Hence, the correct answer is "Pencil - Rub".

questions.question: Human activities that cause climate change on the earth include -
questions.questionHtml: Human activities that cause climate change on the earth include -
questions.solution:
Concept:

  • The type of climate we experience now might be prevailing over the last 10,000 years with minor and occasionally wide fluctuations.
  • The planet earth has witnessed many variations in climate since the beginning.
  • This is generally called climate change.

Explanation:

  • The causes of climate change are many.
  • The most common causes for climate change are population increase, natural phenomena, terrestrial causes, biodiversity loss, and global warming.
  • Human activities also cause climate change on the mass level.
  • The production of carbon dioxide by human activities affects the climate a lot and causes climate change.
  • This increase of carbon dioxide in greenhouse gases causes global warming.
  • Some of the most common activities of human which causes climate change are as follows :
    • Burning of forests
    • Agricultural activities
    • Burning of fossil fuels
    • Construction and manufacturing works
    • The use of aerosol can
    • Urbanization
    • Deforestation

Important Points 

use of aerosol cans:

  • Aerosol cans contain CFC that destroy the ozone layer that protect us from harmful ultraviolet rays.
  • Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) are non-toxic, non-flammable chemicals containing atoms of carbon, chlorine, and fluorine.
  • They are used in the manufacture of aerosol sprays, blowing agents for foams and packing materials, solvents, and refrigerants.

agricultural activities:

  • Irrigated rice or paddy crop cultivation has been identified as one of the leading global agricultural sources of anthropogenic methane (CH4) emissions. 
  • it has been estimated that global rice production is responsible for 11% of total anthropogenic CH4 emissions.
  • Irrigated rice fields are the major source of methane from rice fields.
  • Methane, colourless, odourless greenhouse gas that occurs abundantly in nature and as a product of certain human activities. 

burning of forests:

  • Trees absorb CO2 from the atmosphere and in turn release oxygen back into the atmosphere.
  • Burning down trees will lead to an increase in CO2 concentration in the atmosphere.
  • This in turn will lead to global warming.
  • According to the best current estimate, deforestation is responsible for about 10 per cent of all global warming emissions. 

Thus, human activities that cause climate change on the earth include the use of aerosol cans, agricultural activities, and burning of forests.

questions.question: Which of the following states of India is experiencing mango shower?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following states of India is experiencing mango shower?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Kerala.​Key Points

The monsoon type of climate is characterized by a distinct seasonal pattern over the country. By early June, the low-pressure condition over the northern plains intensified. There are three phases of monsoon showers over the continent, Pre-monsoon shower, Monsoon rainfall, and post-monsoonal rainfall. Additional Information

Pre-monsoon rainfall:

South India:

  • In the south, thunderstorms occur in Kerala and adjoining parts of Karnataka and Tamil Nadu, particularly in the evenings and nights.
  • These pre-monsoonal showers are called by various names:
    • Tea showers in Assam ( they are good for tea, jute, and rice)
    • Mango showers in Kerala and the coastal areas of Karnataka help in the early ripening of mangoes.
    • Cherry Blossoms/ Coffee showers in Kerala and nearby areas (good for coffee plantations)
  • Towards the close of the summer season, pre-monsoon showers are common especially, in Kerala and Karnataka.
  • They help in the early ripening of mangoes and are often referred to as ‘mango showers’

Important Points

North India:

  • Occasionally, the moisture-laden winds are attracted towards the periphery of the trough.
  • A sudden contact between dry and moist air masses gives rise to local storms of great intensity.
  • These local storms are associated with violent winds, torrential rains, and even hailstorms.
  • The thunderstorms which originate over the Chotanagpur plateau are carried eastwards by westerly winds.
  • The areas with the highest incidence of thunderstorms are the north-eastern states, West Bengal, and the adjoining areas of Orissa and Jharkhand.
  • In West Bengal and the adjoining areas of Assam, Orissa, and Jharkhand, the direction of squalls is mainly from the northwest and they are called Norwesters (Squall – a sudden, violent gusty wind).
    • The rainfall brought by northwestern is called spring storm showers.
    • These are often very violent with squall speeds of 60-80km/hour.
    • Large-sized hailstones sometimes accompany these showers and harm the animals and standing crops.
    • The period of maximum occurrence of these storms is the month of Baisakh.
    • These are thus locally called ‘Kal Baisakh (a calamity of the month of Baisakh)’.
    • In Assam, these storms are known as “Bardoli Chheerha or Bordochila”.

questions.question: Which of the following countries are respectively the largest Producers of Coal, Iron Ore and Aluminium?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following countries are respectively the largest Producers of Coal, Iron Ore and Aluminium?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is China, Australia & China.

Key Points

  • Coal: China is the largest producer of coal in the world. The country has significant coal reserves and has been a major contributor to global coal production for many years.
  • Iron Ore: Australia is  the largest producer of iron ore globally. The country's rapid industrialization and infrastructure development have driven substantial demand for iron ore to support its steel industry.
  • Aluminium: China leads in aluminum production as well. The country has a strong presence in the aluminum industry, with a significant share of global production capacity.

Additional Information

  • USA: The United States is a significant producer of coal, but it's not the largest. It has extensive coal reserves and has historically been a major player in the coal industry. The U.S. is also a leading producer of natural gas and oil.
  • Brazil: Brazil is known for its vast reserves of iron ore. It is one of the world's largest producers and exporters of iron ore. The country is also a top producer of agricultural products like soybeans, sugarcane, coffee, and meat.

questions.question: Which type of unemployment is most prevalent in Indian agriculture during the nonsowing season?
questions.questionHtml: Which type of unemployment is most prevalent in Indian agriculture during the nonsowing season?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Seasonal Unemployment.

Key Points

  • Seasonal Unemployment refers to a situation where workers are unemployed during certain seasons of the year, typically due to the nature of their occupation.
  • In Indian agriculture, seasonal unemployment is most prevalent because farming activities are largely dependent on sowing and harvesting seasons.
  • During the non-sowing season, agricultural workers often do not have alternative employment opportunities, leading to temporary unemployment.
  • It is common in agrarian economies like India, where a significant portion of the workforce is engaged in agriculture and allied activities.
  • This type of unemployment highlights the need for diversifying rural employment opportunities to reduce reliance on seasonal agriculture.

Additional Information

  • Disguised Unemployment:
    • It occurs when more people are employed in an activity than required, leading to lower productivity.
    • In Indian agriculture, disguised unemployment is common, especially in small farms where excess labor exists.
    • It is different from seasonal unemployment as it exists throughout the year.
  • Cyclical Unemployment:
    • It is caused by fluctuations in the economy, such as recessions or economic downturns.
    • It is generally not applicable to Indian agriculture, as farming is not directly impacted by economic cycles.
  • Structural Unemployment:
    • This occurs due to a mismatch between skills possessed by workers and the requirements of available jobs.
    • In agriculture, structural unemployment is less common but can arise due to technological advancements reducing the need for manual labor.
  • Government Measures:
    • Programs like the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) aim to reduce seasonal unemployment by providing guaranteed employment during the off-season.
    • The government has also promoted agro-based industries and skill development initiatives to diversify rural employment opportunities.

questions.question: Which key urban feature of Indus Valley cities shows advanced planning with streets intersecting at right angles and covered drains?
questions.questionHtml: Which key urban feature of Indus Valley cities shows advanced planning with streets intersecting at right angles and covered drains?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Grid-pattern layout.

Key Points

  • Grid-pattern layout is a hallmark of Indus Valley Civilization cities, showcasing advanced urban planning.
  • The streets were designed to intersect at right angles, forming a grid system, which ensured organized city planning and efficient movement.
  • Covered drains were constructed alongside streets to maintain hygiene and prevent flooding, reflecting the civilization's emphasis on sanitation.
  • Major cities like Mohenjo-Daro and Harappa displayed this layout, with residential and commercial areas systematically organized.
  • This urban feature highlights the technological and administrative proficiency of the Indus Valley people.

Additional Information

  • Indus Valley Civilization:
    • Citadel & Lower Town: Cities were generally split into a raised "Citadel" (with public/administrative buildings) and a larger "Lower Town" for residences, suggesting social stratification. 
    • Sophisticated Drainage: A covered, underground drainage system connected house drains (from kitchens/bathrooms) to main street sewers, with manholes for cleaning, highlighting focus on hygiene. 
    • Standardized Construction: Uniform, baked bricks of consistent sizes were used for buildings, roads, and drains, showing advanced standardization. 
    • Residential Planning: Houses often had courtyards, bathrooms, and sometimes two stories, with doors opening onto smaller lanes, not main streets. 
    • Public Structures: Large structures like granaries, assembly halls, and the famous Great Bath (Mohenjo-Daro) served communal purposes.

questions.question: Water reabsorption from the distal part of the renal tubule is under the control of which hormone?
questions.questionHtml: Water reabsorption from the distal part of the renal tubule is under the control of which hormone?
questions.solution:
CONCEPT:

Water Reabsorption in the Distal Renal Tubule

  • Water reabsorption in the kidneys, specifically in the distal part of the renal tubule and collecting duct, is regulated by hormones to maintain fluid balance and blood pressure.
  • The hormone primarily responsible for controlling water reabsorption in this region is Vasopressin, also known as antidiuretic hormone (ADH).
  • Vasopressin is secreted by the posterior pituitary gland and acts on the kidneys to increase the permeability of the distal tubule and collecting ducts to water.

EXPLANATION

  • Vasopressin binds to specific receptors on the cells of the distal tubule and collecting ducts.
  • This triggers the insertion of water channels called aquaporins into the cell membranes, allowing water to be reabsorbed back into the bloodstream.
  • This process helps conserve water in the body and concentrates the urine, especially during dehydration or low blood volume conditions.

Additional Information

  •  Renin (Option 1): Involved in the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system, which regulates blood pressure and sodium balance.
  • Oxytocin (Option 3): A hormone involved in uterine contractions and milk ejection, not water reabsorption.
  • Angiotensin (Option 4): A component of the renin-angiotensin system, which indirectly influences water and salt retention but does not directly control water reabsorption in the distal tubule.

Therefore, the correct answer is Vasopressin.

  • Ritual Secrecy: Tradition dictates that the crown must not be exposed to daylight; the head priest must fit it onto the deity while blindfolded or in the dark late at night.
  • It is believed that Garuda (Vishnu's celestial vehicle) brought the crown from the milky ocean after retrieving it from the demon Virochana.

  • Key Patron: The 12th-century Srivaishnava saint Ramanujacharya stayed in Melukote for 12 years and was instrumental in renovating the temple and recovering the processional idol.
  • The temple is situated on the Yadavgiri (Yadugiri) hills. It features a large stepped stone pond called Kalyani Theertha.
  • The temple complex includes unique "sister ponds" known as Akka-Tangi Kola.

Narasipura (Mysuru district), at the confluence of the Kaveri, Kabini, and mythical Spatika Sarovara rivers (Triveni Sangama). It is considered "Dakshina Kashi" and attracts lakhs of devotees for a holy dip.
  4. Mahamastakabhisheka (Shravanabelagola): A key Jain pilgrimage event, this spectacular anointing ceremony for the 57-foot-tall monolithic statue of Lord Bahubali (Gomateshwara) is held once every 12 years. It is a major event for the Jain community.

questions.question: Which of the following statement is not correct regarding Emergency provisions in the constitution of India?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following statement is not correct regarding Emergency provisions in the constitution of India?

options.text: National emergency has no effect on fundamental rights of the citizens.
options.html: National emergency has no effect on fundamental rights of the citizens.

options.text: In National emergency, the relationship of the Centre with all the states undergoes a modification.
options.html: In National emergency, the relationship of the Centre with all the states undergoes a modification.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 1. 

Key Points

  • National Emergency:
    • Under article 352, the President can declare a national emergency when the security of India is threatened by war or external aggression or armed rebellion.
    • There is no maximum period prescribed for its operation.
    • Under this, the relationship of the centre with all the states undergoes a modification.
    • It affects fundamental rights of citizens. Hence, statement 1 is not correct.
    • Lok sabha can pass a resolution for its revocation.
  • President's Rule: 
    • It is mentioned under Article 356 of the Constitution.
    • The maximum period prescribed for its operation is three years.
    • Under this, the relationship of only the state under emergency with the centre undergoes a modification.
    • It does not affect the fundamental rights of citizens.
    • It can be revoked by the President only on his own.​​

Additional Information

  • The Emergency provisions are contained in Part XVIII of the constitution, from articles 352-360.
  • The Constitution stipulates three types of emergencies:
    • National emergency (Article 352): An emergency due to war, external aggression or armed rebellion.
    • Constitutional emergency (Article 356): It is due to the failure of the constitutional machinery in the states. It is also known as President's rule.
    • Financial emergency (Article 360): It is due to the threat to the financial stability or credit of India
  • Financial Emergency:
    • It is mentioned under Article 360 of the Constitution.
    • Article 360 empowers the President to proclaim a Financial emergency if he is satisfied that a situation has arisen due to which the financial stability or credit of India or any part of its territory is threatened.

questions.question: A hemispherical bowl of diameter 16 cm is full of ice cream. Each student in a class is served exactly 6 scoops of ice cream. If the hemispherical scoop is having a radius of 2 cm, then ice cream is served to approximately how many students?
questions.questionHtml: A hemispherical bowl of diameter 16 cm is full of ice cream. Each student in a class is served exactly 6 scoops of ice cream. If the hemispherical scoop is having a radius of 2 cm, then ice cream is served to approximately how many students?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total number of scoops in the bowl = (Radius of bowl ÷ Radius of scoop)3

⇒ Total scoops = (8 ÷ 2)3 = 43 = 64 scoops

Since each student is served exactly 6 scoops:

⇒ Number of students served = 64 ÷ 6 = 10.66

Ice cream can be fully served to a maximum of 10 students with exactly 6 scoops each.

∴ The correct answer is 10 students.

Alternate Method

Given:

Diameter of the hemispherical bowl = 16 cm ⇒ Radius (R) = 16 ÷ 2 = 8 cm

Radius of the hemispherical scoop (r) = 2 cm

Scoops served per student = 6

Formula Used:

Volume of a hemisphere = (2 ÷ 3) × π × radius3

Calculations:

⇒ Volume of the ice cream in the bowl = (2 ÷ 3) × π × 83 = (2 ÷ 3) × π × 512

⇒ Volume of a single scoop = (2 ÷ 3) × π × 23 = (2 ÷ 3) × π × 8

⇒ Total number of scoops = Volume of bowl ÷ Volume of single scoop

⇒ Total number of scoops = [(2 ÷ 3) × π × 512] ÷ [(2 ÷ 3) × π × 8] = 512 ÷ 8 = 64 scoops

⇒ Since each student receives exactly 6 scoops, the number of students = 64 ÷ 6 = 10.66

⇒ Thus, ice cream is fully served to 10 students, leaving exactly 4 scoops remaining in the bowl.

∴ The correct answer is 10 students.

Additional Information

Volume of a Hemisphere

A hemisphere is exactly half of a complete sphere. Its volume formula is V = (2 ÷ 3) × π × r3.

Total Surface Area (TSA) of a Hemisphere

The TSA encompasses the curved surface along with the flat circular base. The formula is TSA = 3 × π × r2.

Volume Proportionality Rule

For any pair of 3D shapes featuring identical proportions (like two spheres or hemispheres), the ratio of their total volumes equals the cube of the ratio of their corresponding linear dimensions.

questions.question: If the sum of first n natural numbers is 55, then the value of n is:
questions.questionHtml: If the sum of first n natural numbers is 55, then the value of n is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Sum of first n natural numbers = n(n + 1) ÷ 2

Given sum is 55, so n(n + 1) = 55 × 2 = 110

We know that 10 × 11 = 110, which represents the product of two consecutive numbers.

Comparing n(n + 1) with 10(10 + 1), we directly get n = 10.

∴ The correct answer is 10.

Alternate Method

Given:

The sum of first n natural numbers = 55

Formula Used:

Sum of first n natural numbers = n(n + 1) ÷ 2

Calculations:

⇒ n(n + 1) ÷ 2 = 55

⇒ n(n + 1) = 110

⇒ n2 + n − 110 = 0

Now, split the middle term to factorise the quadratic equation:

⇒ n2 + 11n − 10n − 110 = 0

⇒ n(n + 11) − 10(n + 11) = 0

⇒ (n − 10)(n + 11) = 0

⇒ n = 10 or n = −11

Since the number of terms (n) cannot be negative, we reject n = −11.

⇒ n = 10

∴ The correct answer is 10.

Additional Information

Sum of squares of first n natural numbers

S = n(n + 1)(2n + 1) ÷ 6

Sum of cubes of first n natural numbers

S = [n(n + 1) ÷ 2]2

Sum of first n odd natural numbers

S = n2

Sum of first n even natural numbers

S = n(n + 1)

questions.question: The average age of a teacher and three students is 20 years. If all three boys are of the same age and the difference between the age of the teacher and the student is 20 years. Then the age of the teacher is equal to:
questions.questionHtml: The average age of a teacher and three students is 20 years. If all three boys are of the same age and the difference between the age of the teacher and the student is 20 years. Then the age of the teacher is equal to:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total age of 4 persons (1 teacher + 3 boys) = 4 × 20 = 80 years.

The teacher is 20 years older than a boy. Subtract this extra age from the total to make all 4 ages equal.

Base total for 4 equal ages = 80 − 20 = 60 years.

Age of 1 boy = 60 ÷ 4 = 15 years.

Age of the teacher = 15 + 20 = 35 years.

∴ The correct answer is 35 years.

Alternate Method

Given:

Average age of 1 teacher and 3 boys = 20 years.

Total number of persons = 1 + 3 = 4.

All three boys are of the same age. Let the age of each boy be S years.

Difference between the age of the teacher and the boy = 20 years, so Teacher's age = (S + 20) years.

Formula Used:

Sum of observations = Average × Number of observations

Calculations:

⇒ Total age of teacher and 3 boys = 20 × 4 = 80 years.

⇒ Sum of ages = Teacher's age + 3 × Boy's age

⇒ (S + 20) + 3S = 80

⇒ 4S + 20 = 80

⇒ 4S = 80 − 20

⇒ 4S = 60

⇒ S = 60 ÷ 4 = 15 years (Age of each boy)

⇒ Age of the teacher = S + 20 = 15 + 20 = 35 years.

∴ The correct answer is 35 years.

Additional Information

Basic Average Formula

The average of a dataset is the sum of its values divided by the number of values. Formula: Average = Total Sum ÷ Count.

Constant Difference in Ages

The difference in age between any two individuals always remains constant throughout their lives, regardless of how many years pass.

Combined Average

If group 1 has N1 items with average A1, and group 2 has N2 items with average A2, the combined average is calculated as (N1A1 + N2A2) ÷ (N1 + N2).

Deviation Method

Averages can also be calculated by assuming a base average and finding the net deviation. If the net deviation is positive, add it to the assumed average after dividing by total items.

questions.question: If a sum triples in 4 years at simple interest, find the time that it would take to become 5 times itself at the same rate of interest.
questions.questionHtml: If a sum triples in 4 years at simple interest, find the time that it would take to become 5 times itself at the same rate of interest.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

In Simple Interest, Interest is directly proportional to Time when Principal and Rate are constant.

For a sum to triple (3 times), Interest = 3 − 1 = 2 units.

For a sum to become 5 times, Interest = 5 − 1 = 4 units.

Time for 2 units interest = 4 years.

Time for 4 units interest = (4 ÷ 2) × 4 = 8 years.

∴ The correct answer is 8 years.

Alternate Method

Given: Time (T1) = 4 years, Amount1 = 3P, Amount2 = 5P (where P is Principal)

Formula: Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) / 100

⇒ SI1 = Amount1 − P = 3P − P = 2P ⇒ 2P = (P × R × 4) / 100 ⇒ R = (2P × 100) / (4P) = 50% ⇒ SI2 = Amount2 − P = 5P − P = 4P ⇒ 4P = (P × 50 × T2) / 100 ⇒ T2 = (4P × 100) / (50P) ⇒ T2 = 400 / 50 = 8 years

∴ The correct answer is 8 years.

Additional Information

Interest Proportionality

In simple interest, the interest earned is directly proportional to time (T) and rate (R) since SI = (P × R × T) / 100.

Amount as n-times Principal

If a sum becomes n times itself, the interest earned is (n − 1) × P. For same rate and principal, T1 / (n1 − 1) = T2 / (n2 − 1).

Rule of SI vs CI

For the first year (or first compounding period), SI and CI are equal if the principal and rate are the same.

questions.question: In a bag, the number of ₹5 coins is 8 more than the number of ₹10 coins but 20% less than the number of ₹2 coins. If the total amount in the bag is ₹270, what is the number of ₹5 coins?
questions.questionHtml: In a bag, the number of ₹5 coins is 8 more than the number of ₹10 coins but 20% less than the number of ₹2 coins. If the total amount in the bag is ₹270, what is the number of ₹5 coins?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Let the number of ₹2 coins be 5y. Then ₹5 coins (20% less) = 4y, and ₹10 coins = 4y − 8.

Total value = 2(5y) + 5(4y) + 10(4y − 8) = 270.

10y + 20y + 40y − 80 = 270 ⇒ 70y = 350 ⇒ y = 5.

Number of ₹5 coins = 4 × 5 = 20.

∴ The correct answer is 20.

Alternate Method

Given:

Number of ₹5 coins is 8 more than the number of ₹10 coins.

Number of ₹5 coins is 20% less than the number of ₹2 coins.

Total amount in the bag = ₹270.

Formula Used:

Total Value = (Value of ₹2 coins) + (Value of ₹5 coins) + (Value of ₹10 coins)

Calculation:

⇒ Let the number of ₹2 coins be 5y.

⇒ Number of ₹5 coins is 20% less = 5y × (80 ÷ 100) = 4y

⇒ Number of ₹10 coins is 8 less than ₹5 coins = 4y − 8

⇒ Total value = (2 × 5y) + (5 × 4y) + 10 × (4y − 8) = 270

⇒ 10y + 20y + 40y − 80 = 270

⇒ 70y = 350

⇒ y = 350 ÷ 70 = 5

⇒ Number of ₹5 coins = 4 × 5 = 20

∴ The correct answer is 20.

Additional Information

Coins and Denominations

The total value of any denomination is calculated by multiplying the face value of the coin with the number of coins (Value = Denomination × Count).

Percentage Relationships

If quantity A is R% less than quantity B, then A = B × (100 − R) ÷ 100. This relationship is often used to find the ratio between multiple quantities quickly.

Linear Equations

Word problems often translate into linear equations format ax + b = c, where solving for the common ratio variable 'y' or 'x' gives the exact values for each parameter.

questions.question: Mohan and Sohan can finish a field work in 50 days, Sohan and Ram in 30 days, while Ram and Mohan in 60 days to finish the same work. How long will they take to finish the work together?
questions.questionHtml: Mohan and Sohan can finish a field work in 50 days, Sohan and Ram in 30 days, while Ram and Mohan in 60 days to finish the same work. How long will they take to finish the work together?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total Work = LCM(50, 30, 60) = 300 units.

Efficiencies: (Mohan + Sohan) = 6, (Sohan + Ram) = 10, (Ram + Mohan) = 5.

Combined efficiency of 2 × (Mohan + Sohan + Ram) = 6 + 10 + 5 = 21.

Efficiency of (Mohan + Sohan + Ram) = 21 ÷ 2 = 10.5 units/day.

Time = 300 ÷ 10.5 = 200 ÷ 7 = 28 4/7 days.

∴ The correct answer is 28 4/7 days.

Alternate Method

Given:

Time taken by Mohan and Sohan = 50 days

Time taken by Sohan and Ram = 30 days

Time taken by Ram and Mohan = 60 days

Formula Used:

Total Work = LCM of all given days

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Number of Days

Time taken = Total Work ÷ Total Efficiency

Person Days Total Work Efficiency
Mohan + Sohan 50 300 6
Sohan + Ram 30 10
Ram + Mohan 60 5

Calculations:

⇒ Sum of given efficiencies = 6 + 10 + 5 = 21 units/day

⇒ 2 × (Efficiency of Mohan + Sohan + Ram) = 21

⇒ Efficiency of (Mohan + Sohan + Ram) = 21 ÷ 2 = 10.5 units/day

⇒ Time taken by all three = Total Work ÷ Total Efficiency

⇒ Time taken = 300 ÷ 10.5

⇒ Time taken = 3000 ÷ 105 = 200 ÷ 7 days

⇒ Time taken = 28 4/7 days

∴ The correct answer is 28 4/7 days.

Additional Information

Work and Wages

Wages are directly proportional to the amount of work done. If people work for the same duration, their wages are distributed in the ratio of their individual efficiencies.

Pipes and Cisterns

The concept is identical to Time & Work. Inlet pipes have positive efficiency (filling) while outlet pipes are considered to have negative efficiency (emptying).

Alternate Day Working

When workers work on alternate days, calculate the work completed in one full cycle (e.g., 2 days for 2 workers) and multiply to reach just below the total work before finishing the rest sequentially.

questions.question: The base of a triangular field is three times its altitude. If the cost of cultivating the field at Rs. 24.4/hect is Rs. 448.35, find its height. (in metres)
questions.questionHtml: The base of a triangular field is three times its altitude. If the cost of cultivating the field at Rs. 24.4/hect is Rs. 448.35, find its height. (in metres)
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total Area = Total Cost ÷ Rate per hectare

Area = 448.35 ÷ 24.4 = 18.375 hectares = 183750 m2

Area of a triangle = ½ × Base × Height

½ × 3h × h = 183750 ⇒ h2 = 122500

h = √122500 = 350 m

∴ The correct answer is 350 m.

Alternate Method

Given:

Base (b) = 3 × Height (h)

Total cost of cultivating = ₹448.35

Rate of cultivating = ₹24.4 per hectare

1 hectare = 10,000 m2

Formula Used:

Area of field = Total Cost ÷ Rate per hectare

Area of triangle = ½ × Base × Height

Calculations:

⇒ Area = 448.35 ÷ 24.4

⇒ Area = 18.375 hectares

⇒ Area in m2 = 18.375 × 10,000 = 183,750 m2

⇒ ½ × Base × Height = 183,750

⇒ ½ × 3h × h = 183,750

⇒ 1.5h2 = 183,750

⇒ h2 = 183,750 ÷ 1.5

⇒ h2 = 122,500

⇒ h = √122500

⇒ h = 350 m

∴ The correct answer is 350 m.

Additional Information

Area of Equilateral Triangle

The area is given by (√3 ÷ 4) × a2, and the height is (√3 ÷ 2) × a, where a is the side length.

Heron's Formula

For a scalene triangle with sides a, b, and c, Area = √[s(s−a)(s−b)(s−c)], where the semi-perimeter s = (a + b + c) ÷ 2.

Hectare Conversion

1 hectare is widely used in land measurement and is equal to exactly 10,000 square meters (m2).

questions.question: In a class the highest marks scored were 67 and lowest were 32. While ca l culating the average of the marks these were erroneously written as 76 and 23. The average of marks of the class will:
questions.questionHtml: In a class the highest marks scored were 67 and lowest were 32. While calculating the average of the marks these were erroneously written as 76 and 23. The average of marks of the class will:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Net change in the total sum = (Sum of erroneous marks) − (Sum of correct marks)

Sum of correct marks = 67 + 32 = 99

Sum of erroneous marks = 76 + 23 = 99

Net change = 99 − 99 = 0

Since the net change in the total marks is zero, the overall average of the class will not change.

∴ The correct answer is Remain unchanged.

Alternate Method

Given:

Highest marks correctly scored = 67

Lowest marks correctly scored = 32

Marks erroneously recorded = 76 and 23

Formula Used:

Change in Average = (Sum of erroneous values − Sum of correct values) ÷ Total number of students

Calculations:

⇒ Actual sum of marks to be considered = 67 + 32 = 99

⇒ Erroneous sum of marks considered = 76 + 23 = 99

⇒ Net change in the sum = 99 − 99 = 0

⇒ Change in average = 0 ÷ Total number of students = 0

⇒ Therefore, the total sum is completely unchanged and the average is unaffected.

∴ The correct answer is Remain unchanged.

Additional Information

Average (Mean)

The average is calculated as the total sum of all observations divided by the number of observations. Average = Sum of elements ÷ Number of elements.

Net Deviation Method

When values are incorrectly recorded or replaced, computing the net deviation directly (Difference = New Sum − Old Sum) helps to quickly find the overall change. Change in average = Net Deviation ÷ Total elements.

Zero Net Deviation

If the sum of correctly recorded values matches the sum of erroneously recorded values perfectly, the net deviation becomes zero. Consequently, there is no change in the sum, meaning the overall average remains completely identical.

questions.question: The income of X is 12% more than that of Y. By how much per cent is Y's income less than that of X?
questions.questionHtml: The income of X is 12% more than that of Y. By how much per cent is Y's income less than that of X?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

If A is R% more than B, then B is less than A by directly using the formula: [R ÷ (100 + R)] × 100%

⇒ Here, X is 12% more than Y, so R = 12

⇒ Required percentage = [12 ÷ (100 + 12)] × 100%

⇒ Required percentage = (12 ÷ 112) × 100%

⇒ Required percentage = (3 ÷ 28) × 100% = 300 ÷ 28 = 75 ÷ 7 = 10 5/7%

∴ The correct answer is 10 5/7%.

Alternate Method

Given:

⇒ The income of X is 12% more than that of Y.

Formula Used:

⇒ Percentage Less = [Difference ÷ Reference Base] × 100%

Calculations:

⇒ Let the income of Y be 100 units.

⇒ Then, the income of X = 100 + 12% of 100 = 112 units.

⇒ Difference in their incomes = 112 − 100 = 12 units.

⇒ We need to find by what percentage Y's income is less than X's income. Here, the reference base is X's income.

⇒ Required percentage = (Difference ÷ Income of X) × 100%

⇒ Required percentage = (12 ÷ 112) × 100%

⇒ Required percentage = (3 ÷ 28) × 100%

⇒ Required percentage = 300 ÷ 28 = 75 ÷ 7

⇒ 75 ÷ 7 = 10 with a remainder of 5, which gives 10 5/7%.

∴ The correct answer is 10 5/7%.

Additional Information

AB Rule in Percentage

If A is R% more than B, then B is [R ÷ (100 + R)] × 100% less than A. Conversely, if A is R% less than B, then B is [R ÷ (100 − R)] × 100% more than A.

Percentage Change and Difference

Percentage change heavily depends on the reference base value. The expression (A − B) ÷ B gives how much A is larger than B, whereas (A − B) ÷ A tells how much B is smaller than A.

Successive Percentage Formula

When a value experiences multiple percentage changes successively (x% and y%), the effective net percentage change is given by the formula: x + y + (x × y) ÷ 100.

questions.questionHtml: A retailer bought 50 kg of Arhar Dal at a discount of 20 %. Besides 2 kg dal was freely offered to him by the wholesaler at the purchase of 50 kg. Now he sells the dal at the marked price to a customer. Find the profit percentage of the retailer?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Let the marked price (MP) of 1 kg dal be 10 units.

Cost Price (CP) for retailer = 50 kg × 8 units (due to 20% discount) = 400 units.

Total quantity to sell = 50 kg + 2 kg free = 52 kg.

Selling Price (SP) of 52 kg at MP = 52 × 10 units = 520 units.

Profit % = [(SP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100 = [(520 − 400) ÷ 400] × 100 = 30%.

∴ The correct answer is 30%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Quantity purchased by the retailer = 50 kg

Discount on purchase = 20%

Free quantity received = 2 kg

Retailer sells the entire dal at the marked price.

Formula Used:

Profit = Selling Price − Cost Price

Profit % = (Profit ÷ Cost Price) × 100

Calculations:

Let the marked price of 1 kg of Arhar Dal be ₹100.

⇒ Marked Price of 50 kg = 50 × 100 = ₹5000

⇒ Discount given to the retailer = 20% of 5000 = ₹1000

⇒ Cost Price (CP) for the retailer = 5000 − 1000 = ₹4000

⇒ Total quantity the retailer gets = 50 kg + 2 kg free = 52 kg

⇒ Since he sells at the marked price, Selling Price (SP) of 52 kg = 52 × 100 = ₹5200

⇒ Profit earned = SP − CP = 5200 − 4000 = ₹1200

⇒ Profit % = (1200 ÷ 4000) × 100

⇒ Profit % = 30%

∴ The correct answer is 30%.

Additional Information

Marked Price and Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price of an article. Selling Price = Marked Price − Discount.

Profit and Loss Calculation

Profit and Loss are strictly calculated on the total out-of-pocket Cost Price unless specified otherwise. Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100.

Buy X Get Y Free

In any promotional scheme where items are given free, the actual effective discount percentage is given by (Free Items ÷ Total Items Received) × 100.

questions.question: The value of : \({x^3-1\over x+3}\div{x^2+x+1\over3x+9}\) = ?
questions.questionHtml: The value of : \({x^3-1\over x+3}\div{x^2+x+1\over3x+9}\) = ?
questions.solution:
Given:

\(\frac{x^3 - 1}{x + 3} \div \frac{x^2 + x + 1}{3x + 9}\) = ?

Formula used:

a3 - b3 = (a - b)(a2 + ab + b2)

Calculation:

\(\frac{x^3 - 1}{x + 3} \div \frac{x^2 + x + 1}{3x + 9}\)

⇒ \(\frac{x^3 - 1}{x + 3} \times \frac{3x + 9}{x^2 + x + 1}\)

⇒ \(\frac{(x - 1)(x^2 + x + 1)}{x + 3} \times \frac{3(x + 3)}{x^2 + x + 1}\)

⇒ 3(x - 1)

∴ The correct answer is option (3).

questions.question: 23 oranges were bought for Rs. 193.20 and sold at the rate of Rs. 108 per dozen. Find the profit percentage correct to one decimal place.
questions.questionHtml: 23 oranges were bought for Rs. 193.20 and sold at the rate of Rs. 108 per dozen. Find the profit percentage correct to one decimal place.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Find the cost and selling price for a single orange to make the calculation simple and direct.

Cost Price (CP) of 1 orange = 193.20 ÷ 23 = ₹8.40

Selling Price (SP) of 1 orange = 108 ÷ 12 = ₹9.00

Profit % = [(SP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100 = (0.60 ÷ 8.40) × 100

Profit % = (1 ÷ 14) × 100 = 7.14% ≈ 7.1%

∴ The correct answer is 7.1%.

Alternate Method

Given:

CP of 23 oranges = ₹193.20

SP of 1 dozen (12 oranges) = ₹108

Formula Used:

Profit = Selling Price (SP) − Cost Price (CP)

Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

Calculations:

⇒ CP of 1 orange = 193.20 ÷ 23 = ₹8.40

⇒ SP of 1 orange = 108 ÷ 12 = ₹9.00

⇒ Profit earned on 1 orange = 9.00 − 8.40 = ₹0.60

⇒ Profit % = (0.60 ÷ 8.40) × 100

⇒ Profit % = (6 ÷ 84) × 100

⇒ Profit % = (1 ÷ 14) × 100

⇒ Profit % = 50 ÷ 7 = 7.1428%

⇒ Correct to one decimal place = 7.1%

∴ The correct answer is 7.1%.

Additional Information

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP). The resulting price is Selling Price (SP) = MP − Discount.

Successive Discounts

If successive discounts of x% and y% are given on an item, the equivalent single discount is given by the formula (x + y − xy÷100)%.

Dishonest Dealer Formula

If a dealer claims to sell goods at Cost Price but uses false weights, Profit % = [(True Weight − False Weight) ÷ False Weight] × 100.

questions.question: In a class there are 40 students (only boys and girls). The number of girls is three-sevenths of the number of boys. Find the number of boys in the class.
questions.questionHtml: In a class there are 40 students (only boys and girls). The number of girls is three-sevenths of the number of boys. Find the number of boys in the class.
questions.solution:
Let number of boys = x, Number of girls = 3x / 7

Total students is x + 3x/7 = 10x/7 = 40 ⇒ x = 28.

Numbers of boys is 28.

questions.question: A boat can go 54 km upstream in 6 hours. If the speed of the stream is 4.8 km/h, then how much time (in hours) will the boat take to cover a distance of 279 km downstream?
questions.questionHtml: A boat can go 54 km upstream in 6 hours. If the speed of the stream is 4.8 km/h, then how much time (in hours) will the boat take to cover a distance of 279 km downstream?
questions.solution:
Speed upstream = 54 km / 6 h = 9 km/h

Speed of boat in still water = 9 km/h + 4.8 km/h = 13.8 km/h

Speed downstream = 13.8 km/h + 4.8 km/h = 18.6 km/h

Time = 279 km / 18.6 km/h = 15 hours

questions.question: A and B can do a work in 8 days, B and C can do the same work in 12 days. A, B and C together can finish it in 6 days. A and C together will do it in?
questions.questionHtml: A and B can do a work in 8 days, B and C can do the same work in 12 days. A, B and C together can finish it in 6 days. A and C together will do it in?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total Work = LCM of 8, 12, and 6 = 24 units.

Efficiencies: (A + B) = 3, (B + C) = 2, and (A + B + C) = 4.

Efficiency of C = (A + B + C) − (A + B) = 4 − 3 = 1 unit/day.

Efficiency of A = (A + B + C) − (B + C) = 4 − 2 = 2 units/day.

Time for (A + C) = Total Work ÷ Combined Efficiency = 24 ÷ (1 + 2) = 8 days.

∴ The correct answer is 8 days.

Alternate Method

Given:

Time taken by A and B together = 8 days

Time taken by B and C together = 12 days

Time taken by A, B, and C together = 6 days

Formula Used:

Total Work = LCM of given days

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time taken

Person Days Total Work Efficiency
A + B 8 24 3
B + C 12 2
A + B + C 6 4

Calculations:

⇒ Efficiency of C = Efficiency of (A + B + C) − Efficiency of (A + B)

⇒ Efficiency of C = 4 − 3 = 1 unit/day

⇒ Efficiency of A = Efficiency of (A + B + C) − Efficiency of (B + C)

⇒ Efficiency of A = 4 − 2 = 2 units/day

⇒ Total efficiency of A and C = 2 + 1 = 3 units/day

⇒ Time taken by A and C = Total Work ÷ Total efficiency

⇒ Time taken by A and C = 24 ÷ 3 = 8 days

∴ The correct answer is 8 days.

Additional Information

Work and Efficiency

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken. If A takes x days and B takes y days to complete a task, the ratio of their efficiencies is y : x.

Pipes & Cisterns Concept

It follows the exact same logic as Time & Work. Filling pipes possess positive efficiency, while emptying pipes or leaks possess negative efficiency.

Alternate Day Work

When people work on alternate days, calculate the combined work completed in one full cycle (e.g., 2 days) and use it to find the total cycles required.

questions.question: The difference between the selling prices with 19% profit and 11% loss is Rs.454.50. What is the cost price of the item?
questions.questionHtml: The difference between the selling prices with 19% profit and 11% loss is Rs.454.50. What is the cost price of the item?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total difference in percentage = Profit % − (−Loss %) = 19% + 11% = 30%

Given that 30% of Cost Price = Rs. 454.50

⇒ 1% of Cost Price = 454.50 ÷ 30 = 15.15

⇒ 100% of Cost Price = 15.15 × 100 = 1515

∴ The correct answer is Rs.1515.

Alternate Method

Given:

Profit = 19%

Loss = 11%

Difference between Selling Prices = Rs. 454.50

Let the Cost Price (CP) of the item be x.

Selling Price at 19% profit (SP1) = x + 19% of x = 1.19x

Selling Price at 11% loss (SP2) = x − 11% of x = 0.89x

According to the question, the difference in selling prices is Rs. 454.50:

⇒ SP1 − SP2 = 454.50

⇒ 1.19x − 0.89x = 454.50

⇒ 0.30x = 454.50

⇒ x = 454.50 ÷ 0.30

⇒ x = 1515

∴ The correct answer is Rs.1515.

Additional Information

Cost Price (CP) & Selling Price (SP)

CP is the price at which goods are bought. SP is the price at which goods are sold. Profit occurs when SP > CP, and Loss occurs when SP < CP.

Effective Change in Profit/Loss

When moving from a loss percentage to a profit percentage on the same base, the total change in percentage terms is the sum of both values (Profit % + Loss %).

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP). The fundamental relation between CP and MP is: MP × (100 − Discount %) = CP × (100 + Profit %).

questions.question: An inlet pipe fills up a cistern in 2 hours, while an outlet pipe empties it in 4 hours. The empty cistern was being filled up with both the pipes open for 1 hour, after which someone closed the outlet. How long will it take in total to fill up the cistern?
questions.questionHtml: An inlet pipe fills up a cistern in 2 hours, while an outlet pipe empties it in 4 hours. The empty cistern was being filled up with both the pipes open for 1 hour, after which someone closed the outlet. How long will it take in total to fill up the cistern?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total capacity = LCM of 2 and 4 = 4 units.

Efficiency: Inlet = +2 units/hr, Outlet = −1 unit/hr.

Volume filled in the 1st hour (both open) = 2 − 1 = +1 unit.

Remaining capacity to be filled = 4 − 1 = 3 units.

Total time = 1 hr (initial) + (3 ÷ 2) hr (remaining filled by inlet) = 2.5 hours.

∴ The correct answer is 2 hours 30 minutes.

Alternate Method

Given:

An inlet pipe fills the cistern in 2 hours.

An outlet pipe empties the cistern in 4 hours.

Both pipes are opened together for the first 1 hour.

Calculations:

Let Total Capacity be the LCM of given times (2 and 4).

Pipe Hours Total Capacity Efficiency
Inlet Pipe 2 4 4 ÷ 2 = 2
Outlet Pipe 4 4 ÷ 4 = −1

⇒ Combined efficiency of both pipes when open = 2 − 1 = 1 unit/hr.

⇒ Part of the cistern filled in the 1st hour = 1 × 1 = 1 unit.

⇒ Remaining capacity to be filled = 4 − 1 = 3 units.

⇒ After 1 hour, the outlet pipe is closed, meaning only the inlet pipe operates with an efficiency of 2 units/hr.

⇒ Time taken by the inlet pipe to fill the remaining cistern = 3 ÷ 2 = 1.5 hours.

⇒ 1.5 hours is equal to 1 hour 30 minutes.

⇒ Total time taken = 1 hour (initial time) + 1 hour 30 minutes (later time) = 2 hours 30 minutes.

∴ The correct answer is 2 hours 30 minutes.

Additional Information

Pipes and Cisterns Basics

An inlet pipe fills a tank, so its work is taken as positive. An outlet pipe (or leak) empties it, so its work is taken as negative.

Net Part Filled in 1 Hour

If an inlet pipe fills a tank in x hours and an outlet pipe empties it in y hours (where y > x), the net part filled in 1 hour is (1/x) − (1/y).

Time and Work Equivalence

Pipes and cisterns problems follow the exact same rules as standard Time & Work problems. Total capacity acts as total work, and the rate of filling/emptying acts as efficiency.

questions.question: Amount on compound interest is doubled to the original amount in 3 years. In how many years will it be eight times its original amount?
questions.questionHtml: Amount on compound interest is doubled to the original amount in 3 years. In how many years will it be eight times its original amount?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

If a sum becomes n times in T years at Compound Interest,

It will become nm times in m × T years.

Here, the sum becomes 2 times in 3 years.

We need the sum to become 8 times, which is 23 times (so m = 3).

Required time = 3 × 3 = 9 years.

∴ The correct answer is 9 years.

Alternate Method

Given:

Principal (P) becomes 2P in Time (T) = 3 years.

Let Rate of Interest be R% per annum.

Formula Used:

Amount (A) = P(1 + R/100)T

Calculation:

⇒ 2P = P(1 + R/100)3

⇒ 2 = (1 + R/100)3    ... (Equation 1)

We need to find the time (T') when the principal becomes 8P.

⇒ 8P = P(1 + R/100)T'

⇒ 8 = (1 + R/100)T'

Since 8 can be written as 23, substitute the value of 2 from Equation 1:

⇒ [(1 + R/100)3]3 = (1 + R/100)T'

⇒ (1 + R/100)9 = (1 + R/100)T'

Comparing the powers on both sides:

⇒ T' = 9

∴ The correct answer is 9 years.

Additional Information

Multiplying Factor in Compound Interest

If a sum of money becomes x times in T years at CI, it becomes xn times in n × T years due to successive compounding.

Simple Interest Linear Growth

Unlike CI, in Simple Interest, if a sum becomes 2 times in T years (i.e., Interest = P), it will become 8 times (Interest = 7P) in 7 × T years since interest remains constant.

Half-Yearly Compounding

When compounded half-yearly, the rate of interest becomes half (R/2) and the time period is doubled (2T). Formula: A = P(1 + R/200)2T.

CI and SI Difference

The difference between Compound Interest and Simple Interest for 2 years on a given principal is calculated as: D = P × (R/100)2.

In the following question, a question is given in Direct speech. Out of the four alternatives, choose the one which best expresses the sentence in Indirect speech

“I’m wearing my lucky pendant, so I should be safe,” she said to him.

options.text: She told him that she is wearing her lucky pendant so she should be safe

options.html: She tells him that she is wearing her lucky pendant so she should be safe.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3)  i.e. She told him that she was wearing her lucky pendant so she should be safe.

Explanation

  • The basic rules for changing or converting direct speech into indirect speech:
    • ​Remove comma and inverted commas.
    • The conjunction 'that' is used in place of commas and inverted commas.
  • Here, reporting verb is in the present continuous tense (Subject +V1st + Object), thus we to change it into the corresponding past continuous tense (Subject +was/were+V1 +ing+ Object).
  • Also, "said to" in "direct speech" is changed into 'told' in "indirect speech".
  • From the above rules, we get the correct sentence as "She told him that she was wearing her lucky pendant so she should be safe."

  • If the first part of the sentence (reporting verb part) belongs to the past tense, the tense of reported speech will change. If the first part of the sentence (reporting verb part) belongs to the present or future tense, the tense of reported speech will not change.
  • The following table will enable us to know how tense changes into Indirect speech:
     
    Direct Speech Indirect Speech
    Present simple (Subject +V1st + Object) Past simple (Subject +V2 + Object)
    Present continuous (Subject +is/am/are+V1 +ing+ Object) Past Continuous (Subject +was/were+V1 +ing+ Object)
    Present perfect (Subject + has/have+V3+Object) Past perfect (Subject+had+V3+Object)
    Past simple (Subject+V2+Object) Past perfect (Subject+had+V3+Object)
    Past Continuous (Subject +was/were+V1 +ing+ Object) Past perfect continuous (Subject +had been+V1 +ing+ Object)
    Future simple (Subject+ will/shall+V1+object) Present Conditional (Subject+ would+V1+object)
    Future Continuous (Subject +will/shall+be+V1 +ing+ Object) Conditional Continuous (Subject +would+be+V1 +ing+ Object)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

EXTRA BITES:

  • When the reporting verb expresses a universal truth, we do not normally change it into the past tense.
    For example:
    • Direct Speech: The President said, ‘All people have equal rights.’
      Indirect Speech: The President said that all people have equal rights.
  • When the reporting verb is in the present or future tense, we do not change the tense of the reporting verb.
    ​    For example:​
    • Direct Speech: He says, 'I will come.'
      Indirect Speech: He says that he will come.

questions.question: A sentence has been given in Active/Passive voice. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active voice. You are requested to keep off the grass
questions.questionHtml:
A sentence has been given in Active/Passive voice. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active voice.

You are requested to keep off the grass

options.text: One should keep off the grass.
options.html: One should keep off the grass.

options.text: You ought to keep off the grass.
options.html: You ought to keep off the grass.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1) i.e. Please keep off the grass.

Explanation:  

  • In Active Voice, a sentence emphasizes subject performing an action.
  • The given sentence is in the passive voice.
  • The use of "please" in the passive voice indicates request.
  • Since the request is made to the person being addressed, "you" should be used.
  • The rest of the options are not in the required passive voice structure, hence they're incorrect. 

Hence, the correct active voice is "Please keep off the grass".

Extra Information: 

  • A sentence that issues a request or gives a command or expresses a desire or wish is called an Imperative sentence.
  • Imperative sentences are addressed without naming the subject. Hence these sentences are without Subject and start with the Principal Verb.

Key Points
  • The passage describes a "fundamental" change in the "geopolitical calculus," specifically noting a "shifting" of the center of gravity from land to sea.
  • "Metamorphosis" (कायाकल्प/रूपांतरण) refers to a change of the form or nature of a thing or person into a completely different one. In the context of global strategy, it perfectly describes the profound structural shift being discussed.
  • "Stasis" (गतिरोध/स्थिरता) refers to a period or state of inactivity or equilibrium. This is the opposite of the "shifting" and "undergone" change mentioned in the text.
  • "Sinecure" (आराम की नौकरी) is a position requiring little or no work but giving the holder status or financial benefit. This is a noun referring to a job, not a process of geopolitical change.
  • "Moratorium" (रोक/पाबंदी) is a temporary prohibition of an activity. There is no mention of a prohibition or suspension in the context of the geopolitical center of gravity.
Therefore, the correct answer is 'Option 4'.
Complete Passage: The geopolitical calculus of the 21st century has undergone a fundamental (1) Metamorphosis, shifting the center of gravity from the continental heartlands of Eurasia to the vast maritime expanses of the Indo-Pacific. For a nation like India, which has historically been preoccupied with the "tectonic" frictions of its land borders and the constant vigilance required by its neighbors, the realization that its economic destiny is inextricably tethered to the stability of the "global commons" necessitates that the Ministry of Defence (2) __________ a more expansive naval posture. A "Blue Water" navy is not merely a collection of sophisticated hulls and high-decibel rhetoric, but a projection of national will across the high seas; however, the transition from a brown-water force is fraught with the (3) __________ of balancing capital-intensive carrier groups against the immediate, often mundane, requirements of coastal security and disaster relief. This strategic pivot requires a recalibration of budgetary priorities, often sparking intense inter-service debates over the allocation of dwindling resources. P- In addition, it is essential for the achievement of sustainable development.

The correct answer is 'PSQR.'

Key Points

    • S follows P because it is talking about requirement of full participation and partnership of both women and men.
    • Q follows S because it is talking about the lack of power and influence.
    • R is directly connected to S6.

  • Therefore, the sequence is 'S1PSQRS6.'
